classification.difficultyReason: Distinguish the next five terms from the first ten, then form and solve simultaneous partial-sum equations.

content.prompt: The sum of the first 5 terms of an arithmetic sequence is 35 and the sum of the next 5 terms is 160. Find the first term and the common difference.

answer.worked:
$S_5=35$; the sum of the next 5 terms is $160$.
$$\begin{align*}S_5=\frac52[2a+4d]&=35\\2a+4d&=14\\a+2d&=7\qquad(1)\end{align*}$$
The sum of terms 6 to 10 is $S_{10}-S_5$.
$$\begin{align*}S_{10}-S_5&=160\\S_{10}&=195\\S_{10}=\frac{10}{2}[2a+9d]&=195\\2a+9d&=39\qquad(2)\end{align*}$$
$(2)-2(1)$:
$$\begin{align*}5d&=25\\d&=5\end{align*}$$
Substitute into $(1)$:
$$\begin{align*}a+10&=7\\a&=-3\end{align*}$$
Therefore $a=-3$, $d=5$.
